findings.reason: one sentence naming which owner is reused (and why the other cannot be) decides whether confinement becomes a third implementation that drifts from the fence's own roots, which is the defect this item exists to catch.
findings.text: §3's Confinement bullet proposes a fresh write-root check while the package already holds two (`sandbox_can_write` at reckon/_backends.py:320, `_within_any` at reckon/_worker_fence.py:983), and it adds a second stdio MCP entrypoint beside `reckon/mcp.py:3837`/`:3846` without saying so

findings.reason: naming the new TOML merge seam, or switching to the argv `-c` form the prototype proved, removes a mechanism the plan has not budgeted.
findings.text: two instances of the same defect. (a) §7 says an `omp` dialect gets "a per-run home under the fence" but names only `_DIALECTS` (reckon/_backends.py:2133); the dialect-keyed registry that actually resolves a run home is `_HARNESS_HOME` (reckon/_worker_fence.py:35, read by `harness_home` at :158 and by reckon/_backends.py:2400), so an entry added only to `_DIALECTS` makes `harness_home()` return None and the run silently keeps the operator's own `~/.omp` — the opposite of what §7 claims. (b) reckon/_worker_fence.py:425 — §5's "seeded codex config with and without the key" requires writing `mcp_servers.anchored` into `CODEX_HOME`'s `config.toml`, but `_seed_harness_entry` copies that file verbatim and returns without touching an existing one, `_merge_harness_entry` (:341) merges JSON only, and the dependency set carries no TOML writer (pyproject: `tomllib` reads only, as at reckon/agent_context.py:350) — while §2's own codex prototype already succeeded by passing `-c mcp_servers.anchored.command=…` on argv, which needs no config write at all

findings.reason: the plan can satisfy this by one sentence per section; without it, §8's "set the default to what the verdict says" leaves both the new surface and the built-in edit tools permanently in place.
findings.text: §3 adds `reckon/anchored_edit.py`, a `reckon-anchored-edit` console script and two MCP tools; §4 adds a flight key (`anchored_edit`), §5 a codex stream-parser branch, §7 an `omp` dialect and an `omp-local` host backend, and no section in the plan states what it retires, merges or brings back from the same family, against public_definitions 2444, cli_options 470, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/anchored_edit.py` hides anchor verification, all-or-nothing atomic replacement preserving mode and line endings, and confinement behind two tools, and §7 extends the existing `Dialect` seam (`reckon/_backends.py:1111`) instead of layering a wrapper over it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 and §7 each add a mechanism whose existing owner is not named: the per-run harness-home registry `_HARNESS_HOME` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:35`) and the codex config seeding `_seed_harness_entry` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:425`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2444, cli_options 470, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §3, §4, §5 and §7 each add surface (a module, a console script, two MCP tools, a flight key, a dialect, a host backend) and none names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 cites its prototype but no search of `reckon/mcp.py` (the package's only stdio MCP entrypoint) or of the existing write-root check `sandbox_can_write` (`reckon/_backends.py:320`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4 and §5 extend `Dialect`/`_ClaudeDialect` (`reckon/_backends.py:1690`, `_DIALECTS` at `:2133`) and `seed_harness_home` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:194`); the separate `reckon-anchored-edit` process is justified because the `reckon` MCP server is user-scope and stays enabled for every worker unnamed (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:325`).
